title: When read PoolSubpage's variant fields, it should lock on PoolSubpage's head lock, instead of PoolArena's lock

timeline.body:
Motivation:

When we read `PoolSubpage`'s variant fields:`doNotDestroy` and `numAvail`, we should lock on `PoolSubpage`'s head subpage, instead of `PoolArena`'s lock. 

Because the writing on `doNotDestroy` and `numAvail` is always under `PoolSubpage`'s head subpage lock.

Modification:

1. Introduced a `int headIndex` field in `PoolSubpage` to locate the head subpage, lock on `PoolSubpage`'s head subpage instead of `PoolArena`'s lock. 
2. This also help to locate head subpage when doing `bytebuf` release. Fixed [13625](https://github.com/netty/netty/issues/13625).

Result:

See above.

timeline.body: What's the relationship to aligned buffers? Why is the test here and not in `PooledByteBufAllocatorTest`?

reply.body: I used to add an assertion in method `PoolChunk.free()`: `assert before_PR_subpge_head == after_PR_subpge_head`, and the `AlignedPooledByteBufAllocatorTest.testCorrectElementSize()` failed assertion, and further found that the issue is related to the `directMemoryCacheAlignment` parameter of `PooledByteBufAllocator`, if the `directMemoryCacheAlignment` is 32, 64..., it will fail the assertion, so I added the new test case here too.

timeline.body: Instead of having a mandatory 3-second wait here, we could make `PoolSubpage.lock` package-private and spin on a `while (!head.lock.hasQueuedThread(t1)) { ... }` condition, until some deadline.

reply.body: But imho, even though, we still need a mandatory wait 'time' or 'times' to decide when to end the `while (!head.lock.hasQueuedThread(t1)) { ... }` looping.
The code can set itself a deadline and check it with `System.nanoTime()`. I think that should suffice to avoid infinite looping.
